function: Learned joint control of task offloading, onboard CPU allocation, and uplink subcarrier allocation in LEO-user links; only the subcarrier allocation is physical layer (pp. 8-9).
system: 6 LEO satellites, 1 GEO, 15 users; OFDM uplink, 24 subcarriers of 400 kHz at 2 GHz; fixed antenna gains, no array or RIS modeled (p. 11, Table II).
method: CTDE-MADDPG multiagent deep RL, one agent per LEO satellite; actor 3 and critic 4 fully connected layers; reinforcement learning, centralized training, decentralized execution (pp. 9-11).
data_channel: Custom Python and STK simulation: link budget with free-space loss, atmospheric loss, log-normal shadowing N(0, 3^2) dB, Shannon rate; no standardized channel or measured data (pp. 6, 11).
test_conditions: Trained 3000 iterations in the Table II setup; evaluated under varied subcarrier bandwidth (100-400 kHz) and LEO computing (1-4 GHz); retraining per point not stated (pp. 11, 13-14).
baselines: Non-learned: random strategy. Learned: CTDE A2C [38], centralized DDPG [31], decentralized DeDDPG [39]; also CTDE-MADDPG without ISL [28], an ablation variant (p. 12).
metrics: Average energy consumption, task success ratio, number of successful tasks (total and per task type), queueing delay per priority level, training reward (pp. 12-14).
complexity: Time complexity of CTDE-MADDPG given as an order expression in layer widths and agent count, Eq. (39); no runtime or FLOPs reported (pp. 10-11).
openness: none; simulation built with Python and STK, no link or statement (p. 11).
q1_support: p. 6: "is calculated using a standard link budget expression"; p. 11: "constructs a simulated SAGIN environment". Custom link budget with log-normal shadowing; no 3GPP TR 38.811 model and no measured data are cited.
q2_support: p. 13: "we evaluate the adaptability of all algorithms under different environments by altering the bandwidth". Only sweeps of subcarrier bandwidth and LEO computing capacity; the paper never states training in one condition and testing in another, nor fine-tuning or transfer.
q3_support: p. 12: "Random Strategy (Random): In the random strategy," (non-learned); p. 12: "The DDPG algorithm, presented in [31],"; p. 13: "32% compared to the centralized DDPG and 76% compared to A2C" (energy). Figs. 7-8 on p. 14 plot Random, A2C, DDPG and DeDDPG.
q4_support: p. 11: "of CTDE-MADDPG is computed by considering the computation required by all agents", followed by the order expression O(U x (...)) in Eq. (39); Section IV-C starts on p. 10.
q5_support: p. 11: "constructs a simulated SAGIN environment" using Python and STK. Custom simulator; no code or data link, DOI, or availability statement anywhere in the paper, and no public channel dataset.
notes: Borderline eligibility: the main focus is offloading and edge-computing resource allocation (above PHY), but the policy also outputs the subcarrier share w of each LEO-user uplink (pp. 8-9, Eq. 31), which the rules count as physical-layer resource allocation in satellite links learned jointly with an above-PHY decision. Included as area 6. The link budget has atmospheric loss and log-normal shadowing (p. 6, Table II) but cites no 3GPP TR 38.811. Contributions list four benchmarks (p. 2) while Section V lists five (p. 12). Table II and Figs. 5, 7, 8 were read as images.
